questions.def: With 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the results.

questions.def: 'Data' is often treated as plural in formal contexts.
questions.question: The data ___ collected meticulously over several years.

questions.def: Committee is acting as a single unit, so singular verb.
questions.question: The committee ___ currently debating the proposed changes.

questions.def: Nouns ending in -ics are often singular.
questions.question: Politics ___ often a contentious topic of discussion.

questions.def: 'A number of' takes a plural verb.
questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today due to illness.

questions.def: Verb agrees with the noun following 'there'.
questions.question: There ___ several reasons for the project's failure.

questions.def: Diseases ending in -s are usually singular.
questions.question: Measles ___ a highly contagious disease.

questions.def: The subject is 'quality', not 'recordings'.
questions.question: The quality of the recordings ___ significantly improved.

questions.def: The verb agrees with the plural noun 'requirements'.
questions.question: What ___ the requirements for the scholarship?

questions.def: Amounts of money are usually treated as singular.
questions.question: Fifty dollars ___ too much to pay for that item.

questions.def: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and verb.
questions.question: Many a student ___ struggled with this concept.

questions.def: The subject is 'all', which is singular in this context.
questions.question: All that ___ needed is a little more effort.

questions.def: When 'jury' acts individually, use plural verb.
questions.question: The jury ___ divided in their opinion.

questions.def: Cake (uncountable) therefore singular verb.
questions.question: Some of the cake ___ gone missing.

questions.def: 'Majority of' takes plural verb if referring to people.
questions.question: A majority of the students ___ in favour of the proposal.

questions.def: Nouns ending in -ics are often singular.
questions.question: Economics ___ a complex field of study.

questions.def: 'None' can be singular or plural, but 'food' is uncountable.
questions.question: None of the food ___ fresh.

questions.def: 'Basics' is plural, therefore needs 'are'.
questions.question: The basics ___ essential for understanding the subject.

questions.def: 'Research' is an uncountable noun in this context.
questions.question: More research ___ needed to confirm these findings.

questions.def: Subject is 'that he enjoys..', use 'is'
questions.question: That he enjoys hiking and camping ___ obvious.

questions.def: Agrees with the plural noun 'reasons'.
questions.question: What ___ his reasons for resigning?

questions.def: 'Members' = plural, therefore 'are' is correct.
questions.question: The elder members of the community ___ showing concern.

questions.def: 'Each' makes the sentence singular.
questions.question: Each and every one of them ___ responsible.

questions.def: Singular verb 'was' agrees with singular 'teacher' when using 'neither/nor'.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ present at the assembly.

questions.def: 'Data' is often treated as plural in academic contexts, thus 'were'.
questions.question: The data ___ collected meticulously over several years.

questions.def: 'Each' is singular, so the verb should be 'has' (Each has...).
questions.question: Each of the participants have received a certificate of completion.

questions.def: 'A number' takes a plural verb: There are reasons.
questions.question: There ___ a number of reasons for the decline.

questions.def: 'A majority of' takes a plural verb when referring to members.
questions.question: A majority of the committee ___ in favor of the proposal.

questions.def: Disciplines like 'economics' take a singular verb: Economics is...
questions.question: Economics ___ a complex social science.

questions.def: With 'there', the verb agrees with the following noun: There seems.
questions.question: There ___ to be some misunderstanding.
